name: Oral testosterone undecanoate (Jatenzo / Kyzatrex)

card.summary: Prescription capsules that deliver testosterone by mouth for diagnosed deficiency; a medical TRT option, not a studied looksmaxxing tool.
card.note: US labels for oral testosterone undecanoate products carry blood pressure warnings; prescription-only controlled substance.

quick.overview:
Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription capsule form of testosterone replacement therapy. Jatenzo was approved by the US FDA in 2019 as the first oral version, followed by Tlando and Kyzatrex in 2022. It is approved for adult men with low or absent testosterone from specific medical causes.

In looksmaxxing and muscle-focused communities it is discussed mainly as a needle-free alternative to injectable or gel TRT. No published trials examine it for appearance or muscle-building in healthy men.
quick.mechanism: Testosterone undecanoate is a prodrug of testosterone. Ordinary oral testosterone is largely cleared by the liver, so these capsules use a lipid-based formulation intended to carry the compound through the lymphatic system and avoid this first-pass loss. Absorption is reported to rise with fatty food and to vary between individuals.
quick.risks: Reported effects include raised blood pressure, acne, hair growth, raised liver enzymes and lipid changes. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and requires a prescription. Testosterone products in general can suppress sperm production.

lead: Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription testosterone replacement therapy taken as a capsule. Restoring testosterone in men who are deficient is associated with the traits people look to testosterone for: muscle mass, body hair, fat distribution, energy and libido, and a review notes the hormone's role in expression of secondary sexual characteristics [4]. Testosterone undecanoate is a prodrug converted to the active hormone in the body, and brand names include Jatenzo, Kyzatrex and Tlando in the United States and Andriol elsewhere [1][2].

The US FDA approved Jatenzo in March 2019 as the first oral testosterone undecanoate product, with Tlando approved in March 2022 and Kyzatrex in July 2022 [1]. They are indicated for adult men with testosterone deficiency from defined medical conditions rather than for age-related decline or cosmetic purposes [1]. Reviews describe the older problem they address: ordinary oral testosterone was limited by liver toxicity and poor bioavailability, so men relied on injections, gels and patches [7][5].

In muscle- and TRT-focused communities such as T Nation, oral undecanoate is discussed as a needle-free alternative to injections, with members comparing the three brands, insurance coverage, lab consistency and blood-count effects [13][14][15][16]. No published trials have tested it in healthy men for physique or facial appearance outcomes; the only registered trial outside male hypogonadism is an early-phase study in menopausal women with low sexual desire [3].

paras: The approved use is testosterone replacement in adult men with low or absent endogenous testosterone [1]. Wikipedia's overview of testosterone medications lists oral undecanoate among several delivery options alongside injections, gels, patches and implants [2].

A comparative review of Jatenzo, Tlando and Kyzatrex reports that trial data show restoration of normal testosterone levels in 80 to 88 percent of patients, with shared risks of hypertension, polycythemia and lipid changes, and notes that dosing regimen, titration requirements and insurance coverage differ between products [7].

A phase 3 randomized trial of Tlando in men with hypogonadism compared efficacy, safety and quality of life with 1.62 percent topical testosterone gel [11]. An open-label trial of men who switched to Jatenzo from other forms of testosterone therapy reported greater satisfaction and similar symptom improvement [10]. A two-year analysis of an oral undecanoate formulation examined efficacy, psychosexual function and safety in hypogonadal men [12]. A meta-analysis cited in a 2023 review pooled placebo-controlled trials and examined body composition, liver function, lipids, blood pressure and symptoms alongside testosterone levels [8].

Plain oral testosterone is extensively metabolised by the liver on first pass, so its oral bioavailability is very low [2]. Undecanoate esters are reported to have bioavailability of roughly 3 to 7 percent that improves with fatty meals, with a short oral half-life of about 1.6 hours and wide variation between individuals [1]. By contrast, the intramuscular undecanoate depot has a half-life measured in weeks [1].

Reviews describe the newer products as using a self-emulsifying lipid-based delivery system with lymphatic absorption, which is intended to avoid the liver problems linked to older oral androgens [9]. Ordinary oral testosterone has long been considered impractical because of rapid first-pass metabolism and short half-life [6]. Jatenzo's development challenges and how the product addresses them are reviewed in the literature [5].

Reported effects of testosterone undecanoate include acne, increased body hair, voice changes in women, hypertension, raised liver enzymes and raised triglycerides [1]. In February 2025 the FDA was reported to have removed cardiovascular-event language from the boxed warning for testosterone products while adding a warning about increased blood pressure [2]. Exogenous testosterone can suppress sperm production, sometimes reversibly [2].

Ciba filed patents on a related testosterone undecylenate combination in the mid-1950s, and oral undecanoate use began in Europe in the late 1970s [1]. US approval of an oral version came only in 2019, followed by two further products in 2022 [1].
Testosterone undecanoate is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and Schedule IV in Canada, and is available by prescription only [1].

sections.h: Use in muscle and TRT communities
paras: On T Nation, men on or considering TRT compare Jatenzo, Tlando and Kyzatrex. One poster notes that Kyzatrex is often cash-pay and argues that oral undecanoate carries little chance of raised red blood cell counts given its pharmacokinetic profile [13]. Another says injections raise hematocrit and hemoglobin more than other routes and points to oral undecanoate as an alternative [15]. A user on Jatenzo describes very consistent lab values and predictable levels through the day [14], while another reports that the capsules at recommended doses reach a mid-range average level [16]. A 2025 review reports hypertension, polycythemia and lipid changes as shared risks across the three products [7].

Clinical trials exist in men with diagnosed hypogonadism: reviews report restoration of normal testosterone in most patients [7], a phase 3 trial against topical gel [11] and an open-label switching study [10]. A 2025 review of testosterone replacement notes that short-acting oral undecanoate might incompletely suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and partially preserve sperm production, while exogenous testosterone in general impairs it [4]. No studies found examining oral testosterone undecanoate for appearance or physique in healthy men. A registered open-label phase 2 study (NCT06082817) plans to test a Kyzatrex regimen in 30 menopausal women with low testosterone and hypoactive sexual desire disorder; it was listed as not yet recruiting [3].

lore.intro: Oral testosterone undecanoate comes up on T Nation in threads about TRT options, blood counts and lab consistency [13][14][15][16].

claims.claim: Oral undecanoate is less likely than injections to raise hematocrit
claims.believers: Posters say injections raise hematocrit and hemoglobin more than other routes and that oral undecanoate has a pharmacokinetic profile that makes high red blood cell counts less likely [13][15].
claims.experts: A comparative review lists polycythemia among risks shared by the three oral products [7].

claims.claim: Oral undecanoate gives very consistent lab values
claims.believers: One user says levels are predictable to within a given half hour after the capsule [14].
claims.experts: Reviews note that absorption depends on food and varies between individuals [1].

claims.claim: Oral products bring levels only to a mid-range
claims.believers: A poster on Jatenzo says capsules at recommended doses average a midpoint level [16].
claims.experts: A review reports eugonadal levels restored in 80 to 88 percent of trial patients [7].

angle.text: For men with diagnosed deficiency, oral testosterone undecanoate aims to bring testosterone back into the normal range, and testosterone is the hormone behind muscle mass, body hair and other masculine traits [4]. People in TRT communities choose it as a needle-free way to do this.
